t: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020
a: Ministry of Labour & Employment (MoLE); Inspector-cum-Facilitator (ICF) at state/central level
sum: The primary workplace-safety statute in India. In force from 21 Nov 2025; it repealed 13 central Acts including the Factories Act 1948, BOCW Act 1996, Contract Labour Act 1970, Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act 1979, Mines Act 1952 and Dock Workers Act 1986. Applies to establishments with 10+ workers (all establishments carrying hazardous activity regardless of headcount).
key: s.3 – single registration of establishment (60 days of applicability); existing registrants update details via Shram Suvidha (Central Rules: Form I, within 6 months of 8 May 2026)
s.6 – general duties of employer: safe workplace, plant, systems, information, annual health examination (as prescribed)
s.10 – notice of accident (death or injury) to ICF; s.11 – dangerous occurrences (even without injury); s.12 – notice of notifiable diseases

s.16–s.22 – National & State OSH Advisory Boards; s.22 Safety Committee (threshold as prescribed, e.g. 500+ workers; hazardous-process factories lower); s.23 Safety Officer (factory 500+, hazardous factory 250+, construction 250+, mine 100+ — verify thresholds in applicable rules)
s.24 – welfare: canteen (100+), crèche (50+), first-aid, drinking water, latrines, welfare officer (250+)
s.25–s.27 – working hours (8 h/day), overtime at twice ordinary wage, rest intervals; s.43 women may work at night with consent and safeguards

Ch. XI – contract labour (threshold 50+); Ch. XII – hazardous processes (compulsory disclosure, safety report, emergency plan, exposure limits); Ch. XIII – building and other construction work; Part on mines
Registers, annual return (unified), inspection by ICF with web-based randomised inspection; graded penalties with compounding; employer may be prosecuted on second offence
note: Labour is a concurrent subject: Central Rules apply where the Central Government is the appropriate Government; otherwise the State's OSH Rules apply. During transition, state Factories/BOCW Rules continue to be used where state OSH rules are not yet final.

t: Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Central) Rules, 2026
sum: Operational rules under the OSH Code for Central-sphere establishments (railways, mines, major ports, oilfields, central PSUs, etc.). Also the model many states are following for their own rules.
key: Registration: Form I (online), certificate in Form III within 7 days; register of establishments in Form V

Rule 7 – Notice of accidents & dangerous occurrences: death – forthwith (electronic + written; inform police and family); injury preventing work 48 h or more and listed dangerous occurrences – within 12 h, Form XI, to ICF and District Magistrate/SDO

Schedule of dangerous occurrences: collapse of lifting machine/crane/hoist, explosion/fire causing damage, bursting of pressure vessel, collapse of structure/scaffold, electrical short-circuit/fire, release of hazardous substance, etc.
Hours of work: 8 h/day, 48 h/week; spread-over; overtime cap per quarter; women night work conditions (transport, CCTV, lighting, batch size)
Health examination, Safety Committee constitution & functions, Safety Officer qualifications, welfare standards, contract labour licence (5-year all-India licence)
note: Where a State Government is the appropriate Government (most private factories and construction sites in Karnataka/Tamil Nadu), use the State OSH Rules; until those are final, the legacy State Factories Rules and BOCW Rules remain the working technical standard.

t: Factories Act, 1948
a: State Chief Inspector of Factories / Director of Industrial Safety & Health
sum: Repealed by the OSH Code w.e.f. 21 Nov 2025, but still essential reading: existing licences, state Factories Rules (Karnataka 1969, Tamil Nadu 1950) and court practice are built on its section numbering, and state rules continue in transition.
key: s.2(cb) hazardous process; First Schedule – hazardous industries
s.7A/7B – general duties of occupier and manufacturers

Ch. IV Safety: s.21 fencing, s.23 young persons on dangerous machines, s.28 hoists & lifts, s.29 lifting machines (competent person test), s.31 pressure plant, s.32 floors/stairs, s.33 pits, s.35 eye protection, s.36 confined space / dangerous fumes, s.37 explosive or inflammable dust/gas, s.38 fire precautions, s.40B Safety Officer (1000+ workers)

Ch. IVA Hazardous processes: s.41A Site Appraisal Committee, s.41B disclosure, s.41C occupier responsibility, s.41F permissible exposure limits (Second Schedule), s.41G safety committee, s.41H right to warn
s.88 notice of accident (death / >48 h absence), s.88A dangerous occurrences, s.89 notifiable diseases (Third Schedule), s.92 penalties
note: Map legacy obligations to OSH Code: s.88 → OSH s.10; s.41G → OSH s.22; s.40B → OSH s.23; s.36 → OSH Code + State Rules on confined spaces.

t: Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996
a: Registering Officer; State BOCW Welfare Boards
sum: Repealed by the OSH Code (21 Nov 2025). Its Central Rules 1998 and the State Rules (Karnataka 2006, Tamil Nadu 2006) remain the most detailed technical safety standard for Indian construction sites and are still referenced by inspectors and contracts.
key: Applied to establishments with 10+ building workers; registration (s.7), registration of workers as beneficiaries with Welfare Board
Ch. VII Safety & Health: s.38 safety committees (500+), safety officers (s.38), notice of accidents (s.39)

Central Rules 1998 technical chapters: excessive noise/vibration, fire protection, emergency action plan, fencing of motors, lifting appliances & gear (test by competent person), runways/ramps, excavation & tunnelling, demolition, scaffolding, ladders, structural frame erection, catch platforms, electrical, explosives, hazardous substances, PPE, medical examination, first aid, canteens, crèches
Rule 36/38 (Central Rules) – helmets, safety belts, protective footwear; Rule 54 – scaffold inspection; Rule 65 – excavation shoring beyond 1.5 m (verify)
note: Welfare cess (1% of construction cost, BOCW Welfare Cess Act 1996) now continues under the Code on Social Security 2020 (Ch. VIII) and State Welfare Boards.

t: Code on Social Security, 2020 (incl. BOCW cess, Employees' Compensation, ESI)
a: MoLE; EPFO; ESIC; State BOCW Welfare Boards
sum: In force 21 Nov 2025. Subsumes the Employees' Compensation Act 1923, ESI Act 1948, BOCW Welfare Cess Act 1996 and others. Governs compensation for occupational injury/disease and the construction welfare cess.
key: Ch. VII Employee's Compensation: employer liability for injury/occupational disease (Third Schedule), report of fatal accidents to Commissioner
Ch. VIII BOCW cess: 1–2% (currently 1%) of cost of construction, paid to State Welfare Board; registration of construction workers as beneficiaries
ESI: accident report to ESIC branch office (24–48 h); medical benefit coverage

t: Contract Labour (Regulation & Abolition) Act, 1970 / Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act, 1979
a: Licensing Officer (now ICF under OSH Code)
sum: Both subsumed in OSH Code Ch. XI. Threshold raised from 20 to 50 contract workers; single all-India contractor licence; principal employer responsible for welfare, wages, and safety of contract labour.
key: Principal employer liable where contractor defaults (wages, PF, safety)
Migrant workers: journey allowance, portability of benefits, toll-free helpline, annual reporting

t: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 & EP Rules, 1986
a: MoEFCC; CPCB; State Pollution Control Boards (KSPCB, TNPCB)
sum: Umbrella environmental statute. Parent Act for MSIHC Rules, Chemical Accident Rules, Hazardous Waste Rules, Noise Rules, C&D Waste Rules, E-waste Rules, Battery Waste Rules, EIA Notification. Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act 2023 decriminalised several offences (adjudicating officer, penalties).
key: s.5 – power to issue directions (closure, stoppage of utilities)
s.7 – no discharge in excess of standards (Schedules to EP Rules)
s.9 – duty to report accidental discharge forthwith to authorities and mitigate
Rule 14 EP Rules – Environmental Statement (Form V) by 30 September each year by units needing consent/authorisation

t: Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 (MSIHC)
a: Chief Inspector of Factories (DISH/DFBISH) for factories; CIF of Dock Safety; AERB etc. per Schedule 5
sum: India's major-accident-hazard (MAH) regime, modelled on Seveso. Applies to industrial activities handling chemicals in Schedule 1 (named chemicals & threshold quantities), Schedule 2 and Schedule 3.
key: Rule 4 – general duty: identify major accident hazards, provide information, training, equipment
Rule 5 – notify major accident within 48 h (Schedule 6); investigation and report
Rule 7/8 – notification of site (Schedule 7) at least 3 months before commencing; updating
Rule 10 – Safety Report (Schedule 8) for Schedule 3 threshold units; updated every 3 years or on modification
Rule 12 – safety audit annually by competent person; Rule 13 – on-site emergency plan (rehearsed every 6 months); Rule 14 – off-site emergency plan by District Collector/Emergency Authority
Rule 15 – information to public; Rule 17 – Material Safety Data Sheet (Schedule 9) for every hazardous chemical; labelling; Rule 18 – import
note: Draft MSIHC Rules 2024/2025 proposing GHS-aligned classification were circulated by MoEFCC; verify current status.

t: Chemical Accidents (Emergency Planning, Preparedness and Response) Rules, 1996
a: Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups; District Collector
sum: Sets up the four-tier crisis-group structure for chemical emergencies and obliges MAH units to feed information and participate in off-site planning and mock drills.
key: Rule 9 – District Crisis Group chaired by District Collector; off-site plan rehearsal
Rule 10 – Local Crisis Group at industrial pocket level; MAH units supply information
Occupier must assist in off-site emergency plan, conduct full-scale mock drill at least once a year

t: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016
sum: Generation, storage (max 90 days), transport, treatment and disposal of hazardous waste (Schedule I/II/III); manifest system; authorisation (Form 1/2); annual returns (Form 4 by 30 June); accident reporting (Form 11).
key: Rule 6 – authorisation from SPCB; Rule 8 – storage ≤ 90 days; Rule 16 – labelling; Rule 18 – manifest (Form 10) and transport; Rule 20 – record (Form 3) & annual return (Form 4)
Rule 23 – accident during handling: report immediately to SPCB in Form 11
Co-processing / TSDF / recycler registration

t: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 & Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
sum: Consent to Establish (CTE) before construction and Consent to Operate (CTO) before commissioning for Red/Orange/Green/White category industries (CPCB categorisation). Stack/effluent standards, continuous monitoring (OCEMS) for 17 categories.
key: Water Act s.25/26 – consent for discharge; Air Act s.21 – consent to operate in air-pollution control area
Construction sites: dust control, DG set stack height & noise limits, STP for labour colonies
Non-compliance: closure directions under s.33A/31A; Jan Vishwas 2023 penalty regime

t: Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000
sum: Ambient noise limits by zone (dB(A) Leq): Industrial 75 day / 70 night; Commercial 65/55; Residential 55/45; Silence 50/40. Night = 10 pm–6 am. Construction equipment and DG sets also have source limits under EP Rules Schedule VI.
key: No loudspeaker/construction noise above limits at night without permission
DG sets: noise limit 75 dB(A) at 1 m (≤1000 kVA, EP Rules); acoustic enclosures
Occupational limit (Factories Act Sch. II / OSH rules): 90 dB(A) 8-h TWA; OSHA PEL 90 dB(A), action level 85 dB(A)

t: Environment (Construction and Demolition) Waste Management Rules, 2025
a: MoEFCC; CPCB; Urban Local Bodies; SPCB
sum: Supersedes the C&D Waste Management Rules 2016; effective 1 April 2026. Introduces Extended Producer Responsibility-style obligations for large generators (projects ≥ 20,000 m² built-up or demolition of similar size), mandatory C&D waste management plans, segregated storage, use of recycled products, and online portal reporting.
key: Generator must segregate (concrete, soil, steel, wood, plastics), store within site, and hand over to authorised processor; no dumping on roads/drains/water bodies
Large projects: C&D waste management plan submitted with building permit; targets for use of recycled material in new construction
Registration on CPCB portal; annual returns; environmental compensation for violation
note: Local-body bye-laws (BBMP, Greater Chennai Corporation) impose dust-control, barricading and debris-transport conditions in addition.

t: EIA Notification, 2006 (as amended) – Prior Environmental Clearance
sum: Prior EC needed before construction for listed projects: Item 8(a) building/construction ≥ 20,000 m² built-up; 8(b) townships ≥ 50 ha or ≥ 1,50,000 m²; industrial projects by sector thresholds (chemicals, cement, metallurgy, power, etc.). EC conditions typically include dust, noise, worker welfare, STP, rainwater harvesting and six-monthly compliance reports.
key: Six-monthly compliance report to Regional Office of MoEFCC
EC conditions are legally binding; violation → EP Act action

t: Petroleum Act, 1934 & Petroleum Rules, 2002
sum: Storage, transport and handling of petroleum Class A (flash point < 23 °C), B (23–65 °C), C (65–93 °C). Licence thresholds (e.g. Class A > 30 L, Class B > 2,500 L in bulk) and safety distances, earthing, flameproof electricals (IS/IEC 60079), no smoking, fire-fighting.
key: Form XIV/XV licences; Rule 118 – hot work within licensed premises only with gas-free certificate
Accident in licensed premises: notify PESO Chief Controller and local police forthwith
Diesel storage at construction sites (Class B): licence if > 2,500 L; bunding, spill kit, extinguishers

t: Explosives Act, 1884 & Explosives Rules, 2008; Ammonium Nitrate Rules, 2012
sum: Manufacture, possession, use, transport and sale of explosives. Blasting on construction/quarry sites needs licensed magazine, licensed blaster/shot-firer, blasting plan, and local police/DM permission.
key: Licence Forms LE-1 to LE-5; magazine construction and distance tables
Blasting: siren, 500 m exclusion (typical), misfire procedure (IS 4081), vibration limits (DGMS circular 7 of 1997 for structures)
Accident notice to Chief Controller of Explosives forthwith

t: Gas Cylinders Rules, 2016 & Static and Mobile Pressure Vessels (Unfired) Rules, 2016
sum: Filling, possession, storage and transport of compressed gas cylinders (oxygen, acetylene, LPG, CO2, argon) and bulk pressure vessels (LPG bullets, ammonia, chlorine tonners). Periodic hydrostatic testing, colour coding (IS 4379), valve protection, storage separation (oxidisers ≥ 6 m / fire wall from fuel gases).
key: Storage of > 200 cylinders needs PESO licence (verify current threshold)
SMPV(U): licence (Form III), safety relief valve testing, competent-person inspection every 5 years, fire protection
Gas Cylinders (Amendment) Rules 2025 – verify changes for composite/hydrogen cylinders

t: Boilers Act, 2025 & Indian Boiler Regulations, 1950
a: Central Boilers Board; State Chief Inspector of Boilers (Karnataka DFBISH / Tamil Nadu DISH-Boilers)
sum: Boilers Act 2025 replaced the Boilers Act 1923 (effective 1 May 2025) with decriminalised penalties and third-party inspection. Registration, annual certificate of inspection, boiler attendant/operator certification (BOE), economiser/steam pipeline inspection.
key: No boiler to be used without certificate; hydraulic test; safety valve setting
Accident/explosion: report to Chief Inspector of Boilers within 24 h; do not disturb scene
Operator: Boiler Attendant (1st/2nd class) / BOE depending on heating surface

t: Electricity Act, 2003 & CEA (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations, 2023
a: Central Electricity Authority; State Chief Electrical Inspector (CEIG)
sum: Safety regulations for generation, transmission, distribution and use of electricity. 2023 regulations superseded the 2010 regulations (verify transitional provisions). Covers earthing, clearances from overhead lines, approval of HT installations, periodic inspection, electrical accidents.
key: Approval of CEIG before energising HT/EHT installations and multi-storey buildings (>15 m) electrical installations
Vertical/horizontal clearances from overhead lines; working near live lines; shutdown & permit-to-work
Electrical accident: notify Electrical Inspector within 48 h (Form A), fatal – immediately
Earthing (IS 3043), ELCB/RCD 30 mA for portable tools (IS 732), lightning protection (IS/IEC 62305)

t: Mines Act, 1952 / Mines Rules 1955 / Metalliferous Mines Regulations 1961 / Coal Mines Regulations 2017
sum: Mines Act subsumed in OSH Code (Part on mines); Regulations continue. Relevant to quarries, crushers and earth-extraction supplying construction. DGMS circulars on blasting vibration, HEMM, dump design, mine managers' certification.
key: Quarry: mine manager (permanent 2nd class), notice of opening, DGMS approval of plans
Benches, haul roads (gradient 1 in 16), dump slope; blasting by competent person
Fatal/serious accident: notice to DGMS Regional Inspector forthwith; Form IV-A

t: Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991
sum: Owners handling hazardous substances above notified quantities must carry public liability insurance to pay immediate no-fault relief to victims of accidents; contribute to Environmental Relief Fund.
key: Accident report to Collector; relief application within 5 years

t: Disaster Management Act, 2005 (as amended 2025) & NDMA Guidelines
a: NDMA; State DMAs (KSDMA, TNSDMA); District DMAs
sum: National framework for disaster preparedness. NDMA Guidelines on Chemical (Industrial) Disasters 2007, Fire Safety, Heat Wave Action Plans, Lightning. Industrial sites feed into District Disaster Management Plans.
key: District Collector powers during emergency (s.34); requisition of resources
Heat action plans (TN and Karnataka) inform outdoor-work scheduling

t: National Building Code of India 2016 (SP 7) – Part 4 Fire & Life Safety; Part 7 Construction Management, Practices & Safety
a: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS); adopted by state building rules
sum: Part 4 sets occupancy-based fire protection (travel distance, refuge areas, fire pumps, sprinklers above 15 m / by occupancy). Part 7 covers construction practices and safety: scaffolds, formwork, excavation, demolition, temporary works, site organisation, safety in construction (clause 11), and is mandatory where adopted by state building rules (TN CDBR 2019; Karnataka Model Building Bye-laws).
key: Part 7 Sec. 2 – Construction practices; Sec. 3 – Demolition; Sec. 4 – Safety management (safety plan, safety officer, training, PTW, PPE)
Part 4 – high-rise definition ≥ 15 m; fire NOC from State Fire Service

t: BIS Codes for Construction Safety (IS 3696, IS 4014, IS 3764, IS 4130, IS 4081, IS 13430, IS 7205, IS 13367, IS 14489, IS 3786)
sum: Key Indian Standards referenced in BOCW/state rules and contracts.
key: IS 3696 Pt 1 (scaffolds) & Pt 2 (ladders) – safety code
IS 4014 Pt 1/2 – steel tubular scaffolding
IS 3764 – excavation work safety code; IS 4130 – demolition of buildings; IS 4081 – blasting and drilling in construction
IS 7205 – safety code for erection of structural steelwork; IS 7969 – handling & storage of building materials; IS 7293 – handling cement
IS 13430 – safety during additional construction/alteration of existing buildings; IS 13416 Pt 1–5 – preventive measures against hazards (falls, falling objects, heat, fire, drowning)
IS 13367 Pt 1 – safe use of cranes; IS 807 / IS 3177 – crane design; IS 4573 – power-driven mobile cranes
IS 14489 – code of practice on occupational safety and health audit; IS 3786 – computation of injury frequency/severity rates
IS 18001:2007 – OHSMS (Indian standard; largely replaced in practice by IS/ISO 45001)

t: BIS PPE & Equipment Standards (IS 2925, IS 15298, IS 3521, IS 5983, IS 9167, IS 9473, IS 2190, IS 15683, IS 3043, IS 732, IS 5216)
sum: Procure PPE and site equipment to these marks (ISI mark where under compulsory certification — safety helmets, footwear, goggles are under Quality Control Orders).
key: IS 2925 – industrial safety helmets (QCO); IS 15298 Pt 2 – safety footwear (QCO); IS 5983 – eye protectors; IS 9167 – ear protectors; IS 9473 – respiratory filters; IS 3521 Pt 1–3 – industrial safety harness, lanyards, anchors (fall arrest)
IS 2190 – selection, installation & maintenance of portable fire extinguishers; IS 15683 – portable extinguishers performance
IS 3043 – earthing; IS 732 – electrical wiring installations; IS 5216 – safety procedures in electrical work; IS 13252 – IT equipment safety
IS 4379 – colour coding of gas cylinders; IS 818 – safety in welding; IS 3016 – fire precautions in welding/cutting

t: OISD Standards (OISD-STD-105 Work Permit, 116/117 Fire Protection, 118 Layouts, 160 LPG, GDN-206 Safety Audit)
sum: Mandatory for the Indian oil & gas sector and widely adopted by petrochemical and process plants as good practice. OISD-STD-105 is the de-facto Indian permit-to-work benchmark.
key: OISD-STD-105 – work permit system (hot, cold, confined space, excavation, electrical, vehicle entry); gas test limits (LEL 0% for hot work in process areas)
OISD-STD-118 – inter-unit safety distances; OISD-STD-116 – fire protection in refineries
OISD-GDN-206 – external safety audit; OISD-STD-163 – process safety management

t: Atomic Energy (Radiation Protection) Rules, 2004 – Industrial Radiography & Nucleonic Gauges
sum: NDT radiography on sites (pipeline welds, pressure vessels) needs AERB-licensed agency, Radiological Safety Officer, certified radiographers, cordoned area (boundary 1 µSv/h), source storage pit, transport approval, and personnel dosimetry (TLD).
key: AERB Safety Code AERB/RF-IR/SC-1 – industrial radiography; e-LORA licensing
Radiography generally at night or in enclosed bays; public dose limit 1 mSv/yr; worker 20 mSv/yr (avg over 5 yrs)

t: Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 (amended 2016)
sum: No child < 14 in any occupation; adolescents (14–18) barred from hazardous occupations/processes (mines, inflammable substances/explosives, hazardous processes under Factories/OSH Code – includes construction). Age verification records at site gate.
key: Penalty: imprisonment 6 months–2 years and/or fine; repeat offence stricter
Construction, demolition, brick kilns, welding, chemicals listed as hazardous for adolescents

t: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 & CMV Rules 1989 – Site Vehicles and Earth-Moving Equipment
sum: Registration and fitness of tippers, transit mixers, mobile cranes; construction equipment vehicles (CEV) registration; driver licensing; overloading; reversing alarms/AIS standards; working near public roads (IRC SP 55 traffic management during construction).
key: CEV: registration, fitness, trained operator; IRC:SP:55 – temporary traffic control; IRC 35 road markings
Speed limits on site (typically 10–20 km/h) set by site rules

t: GHS / Safety Data Sheets in India – MSIHC Rule 17 & Schedule 9, draft GHS alignment
sum: India has not fully mandated UN GHS; MSIHC Rule 17 requires an MSDS in the Schedule 9 format and labelling. Draft MSIHC amendments propose GHS-based classification. Industry practice: supply 16-section GHS SDS (IS/ISO 11014) and GHS pictogram labels.
key: Use 16-section SDS (ISO 11014 / ANSI Z400.1 / UN GHS Annex 4) as the working format
Label: product identifier, signal word, hazard pictograms, H & P statements, supplier

t: National Policy on Safety, Health and Environment at Workplace (2009) & DGFASLI
a: Directorate General Factory Advice Service & Labour Institutes (DGFASLI)
sum: National policy framework; DGFASLI issues model rules, safety guidance, and runs Central Labour Institutes (Mumbai, Kanpur, Chennai, Kolkata, Faridabad). Dock Safety Inspectorate for ports.
key: Model Factories Rules (reference for state rules); Guidance on safety audit, HIRA, process safety
Dock Workers (Safety, Health & Welfare) Regulations 1990 – port/cargo handling (subsumed into OSH Code)

t: Shram Suvidha Portal – Unified Registration & Annual Returns
sum: Single online portal for Labour Identification Number (LIN), registration under OSH Code/Central Rules (Form I), unified annual return, and inspection reports for central-sphere establishments; many states integrate via their own portals (Karnataka e-Shrama/Seva Sindhu; Tamil Nadu DISH online).
key: Update existing registration details within 6 months of 8 May 2026 (i.e. by 8 Nov 2026) – Central Rules

t: Karnataka Factories Rules, 1969
a: Department of Factories, Boilers, Industrial Safety & Health (DFBISH / FBISH), Govt of Karnataka – e-Surakshate portal
sum: State rules under the Factories Act: approval of plans, licensing (Forms), hazardous process chapter (Rules 88-A to 88-P: H&S policy, OHC, ambulance van, Safety Committee 88-B, chemical disclosure), machine guarding (Rule 56 Schedules I–VII), lifting machines (Rules 58/59, Forms 6/7), pressure vessels (Rule 61, Form 8), thermic-fluid heaters (Rule 65-B), PPE (Rule 65/88), fire (Rule 66), ventilation (Rule 19), dangerous operations (Rule 129, 26+ Schedules), welfare. Remain the working technical standard until the OSH (Karnataka) Rules are final.
key: Approval of plans & licence (online via DFBISH/Seva Sindhu); self-certification scheme 2024 for low-risk factories
Lifting machines/tackles tested every 12 months by competent person; pressure vessels (Rule 61) hydraulic test; hoists/lifts 6-monthly
Dangerous operations schedules (lead, chrome, electroplating, sand-blasting, solvents, asbestos, foundry, pesticides etc.) – medical examination by certifying surgeon
Notice of accident: fatal – immediate (phone/online) + written report within time prescribed (Form 18 – verify); non-fatal >48 h – within 24 h; dangerous occurrence – within 4 h (verify)
Safety Officer (Rule 100-series) qualifications; Safety Committee; occupational health centre for hazardous units (Rule 85-series)
note: Form numbers and timelines are state-specific — confirm against the current consolidated rules on the DFBISH site.

t: Karnataka Factories (Safety Audit) Rules, 2024
sum: Mandatory periodic safety audit of factories (hazardous-process / MAH units and other notified categories) by empanelled external safety auditors, with audit report submission and closure of findings.
key: Audit by Chief Inspector-recognised auditor; frequency (annual for hazardous, as notified for others – verify)
Report in prescribed format; compliance action plan; follow IS 14489 methodology

t: Factories (Karnataka Amendment) Act, 2023
sum: Allowed daily working hours up to 12 h (within 48 h/week) with consent, raised quarterly overtime limit to 145 h, and permitted women on night shifts (7 pm–6 am) subject to safeguards (transport, CCTV, security, batches, written consent). Now read alongside OSH Code s.25–s.27, s.43.
key: Women night shift conditions: free transport with security, well-lit premises, not less than 10 women per shift (typical), anti-harassment committee
Spread-over up to 12 h; compensatory rest

t: Draft Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (Karnataka) Rules, 2026
a: Labour Department, Govt of Karnataka (Notification LD 245 LET 2021, 23 Jan 2026)
sum: Draft state rules under the OSH Code published 23 Jan 2026 (objections to 9 Mar 2026). Cover registration, employer duties (annual health exam, accident/dangerous-occurrence notice, disease notice), Safety Committee & Safety Officer, working hours, registers & returns, Inspector-cum-Facilitator, women's night work, dangerous operations. Final notification status: verify with Labour Department.
key: Until final: apply Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 / Karnataka BOCW Rules 2006 technical provisions, and OSH Code sections directly
Expect Form numbering aligned to Central Rules (Form XI accident notice)

t: Karnataka Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 2006
a: Labour Department; Karnataka Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (KBOCWWB)
sum: State construction safety rules: registration of establishments, cess (1%), worker registration, and detailed safety chapters mirroring Central Rules 1998 (scaffolds, excavation, demolition, lifting appliances, electrical, PPE, welfare, first aid, canteen, crèche, safety committee/officer).
key: Safety Officer for sites with 500+ workers (Rule – verify); Safety Committee; site safety plan
Lifting appliance test certificate (Form – verify) by competent person every 12 months; daily checks
Accident notice to Registering Officer/Inspector; fatal – within 4 h (verify) and police
Welfare: drinking water, latrines (1 per 20 up to 100), washing, rest shed, crèche (50+ women workers), first-aid boxes, ambulance arrangement

t: Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments Act, 1961 (amended 2026)
sum: Covers offices, site offices, IT and commercial premises. The Karnataka Shops and Commercial Establishments (Amendment) Act 2026 (notified 4 Sept 2026) removes duplicate registration for establishments registered under OSH Code s.3 and applies the SS Code mutatis mutandis.
key: Women night work: driver antecedent verification, route planning, vehicle monitoring (stricter than OSH rules)
Working hours 9/day, 48/week; OT 2x

t: Karnataka Fire Force Act, 1964 & Karnataka State Fire and Emergency Services NOC Rules
a: Karnataka State Fire and Emergency Services (KSFES)
sum: Fire NOC (clearance) for buildings ≥ 15 m high and specified occupancies (industrial, hazardous storage, assembly); provisional NOC at plan stage, final NOC before occupancy; annual renewal/ inspection. Fire-fighting requirements per NBC Part 4.
key: Industrial buildings: fire hydrant ring main, extinguishers (IS 2190), automatic detection; high-hazard – sprinklers, foam
Site: fire extinguishers within 15 m of hot work; fire watch; emergency assembly point

t: Karnataka Lifts, Escalators and Passenger Conveyors Act, 2012 & Rules
a: Chief Electrical Inspector to Government, Karnataka
sum: Licence to erect and operate lifts/escalators (including temporary builder's hoists where applicable under BOCW rules); annual inspection; competent person certificate; accident reporting to Electrical Inspectorate.
key: Erection permission → inspection → licence to work; renewal; AMC by licensed agency
Passenger/material hoists on sites: BOCW rules + IS 4014/IS 3696 for hoistways; operator competence

t: Karnataka State Pollution Control Board – Consents, Authorisations & Construction Dust Guidelines
sum: CTE/CTO under Air & Water Acts via the XGN portal; HW authorisation; lake & buffer-zone protection norms (NGT/KSPCB mandates around Bellandur, Varthur and Peenya industrial basins); mandatory OCEMS for the 17 highly polluting categories; mandatory STP dual-piping reuse for commercial/industrial complexes in Bengaluru; authorised TSDFs at Dobbaspet and Harohalli; C&D waste; noise (Bengaluru construction-noise regulation); Bengaluru dust-control checklist (barricading ≥ 3 m, covered transport, wheel wash, water sprinkling, no on-site burning).
key: Red/Orange/Green/White categories; consent validity by category; bank guarantee for non-compliance
Diesel generator: KSPCB noise & emission norms; DG > 1 MVA needs separate consent

t: Karnataka Model Building Bye-laws / BBMP Building Bye-laws & Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961
a: BBMP / Urban Local Bodies / BDA; Urban Development Department

t: Energy Conservation Act, 2001 (as amended 2022) & Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)
a: Ministry of Power; Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE); State Designated Agencies (KREDL – Karnataka; EMC – Tamil Nadu)
sum: Parent law for energy efficiency and, since the 2022 amendment, for the Indian carbon market. Designated consumers (energy-intensive units above notified thresholds in sectors such as cement, iron & steel, aluminium, fertilizer, pulp & paper, chlor-alkali, textiles, refineries, petrochemicals, thermal power, DISCOMs, railways, large buildings) must appoint an energy manager, get mandatory energy audits by BEE-accredited auditors, file annual returns and meet PAT (Perform, Achieve and Trade) targets. The 2022 amendment enables the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, mandates non-fossil energy use for designated consumers, and renames ECBC as the Energy Conservation and Sustainable Building Code.

t: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023 (as amended) – Indian Carbon Market (ICM)
a: BEE (administrator); Ministry of Power; CPCB (compensation); Grid Controller of India (registry); CERC (trading on power exchanges)
sum: India's compliance carbon market. GHG emission intensity (GEI) targets notified under the EC Act for obligated entities: aluminium, cement, chlor-alkali, pulp & paper (8 Oct 2025, 282 plants) and petroleum refineries, petrochemicals, textiles (16 Jan 2026) — 490 entities in 7 sectors; iron & steel targets issued as a draft (G.S.R. 517(E), 26 June 2026, 255 units) and fertilizer still pending. Targets apply to FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 against a FY2023-24 baseline (about 40% of the reduction due in year one). Over-performers receive Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs) to sell; under-performers must buy and surrender CCCs; an offset mechanism lets non-obligated entities register projects.
key: Obligated entity: monitoring plan approved by BEE; monthly monitoring; verified GHG emission report by an Accredited Carbon Verification Agency (ACVA) within 4 months of FY end (FY2025-26 → 31 Jul 2026; FY2026-27 → 31 Jul 2027)
CCC issuance on the ICM registry (BEE procedure date 30 Sep 2026 for the first cycle); trading only on CERC-registered power exchanges (first trades expected late 2026)
Shortfall: buy CCCs; failing that, environmental compensation by CPCB equal to twice the average CCC price of the cycle; shortfall recorded
Scope 2 for CCTS uses the CEA grid emission factor (CO2 Baseline Database v20: 0.727 tCO2/MWh for FY2023-24 weighted average; check v21)
Links to BRSR (Principle 6 disclosures) and to EU CBAM (verified installation data reusable)
note: Sector coverage, baselines and deadlines change by notification — the statement above reflects reporting up to early Oct 2026; confirm the current GEI notification for your sector.

t: SEBI Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) & BRSR Core
sum: Mandatory ESG disclosure for the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation (since FY2022-23), structured on the nine NGRBC principles. BRSR Core (July 2023 circular) is a subset of KPIs across nine attributes — GHG emissions, energy, water, waste, inclusive development (incl. OSH), wages, gender diversity, customer complaints and business openness — subject to reasonable assurance / 'assessment', phased in: top 150 (FY2023-24), top 250 (FY2024-25), top 500 (FY2025-26) and all top 1,000 from FY2026-27. Value-chain disclosures for partners each contributing ≥ 2% of purchases/sales apply from FY2026-27 (assessment or assurance).
key: Principle 3 (employee well-being) and Principle 6 (environment): safety incidents (LTIFR per million hours, fatalities, recordable injuries), safety-management-system coverage, health & safety training, GHG Scope 1/2 (and 3 leadership indicator), energy intensity, water, waste, air emissions
BRSR Core attribute: 'Enabling a safe, healthy workplace' – OSH KPIs must be auditable: incident registers, hours worked, training records
Data must reconcile with statutory registers (OSH Code registers, Form V, HW Form 4) — assurance providers trace to source
Dec 2024/2025 SEBI amendments: 'assessment or assurance' option, green credits disclosure, ESG rating providers (ERP) regulated

t: EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) – Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as amended by (EU) 2025/2083
a: European Commission; EU national competent authorities; authorised CBAM declarants (EU importers)
sum: Definitive regime from 1 Jan 2026 for cement, iron & steel (incl. listed downstream articles), aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen. EU importers must be authorised declarants and will buy CBAM certificates priced on EU ETS auctions (certificate sales open 1 Feb 2027; first annual declaration and surrender for 2026 imports due 30 Sep 2027). De minimis: importers at or below 50 t/yr of the goods (not electricity/hydrogen) are exempt. Indian exporters feel it through buyer demands for installation-level verified emissions data; default values carry mark-ups (10% in 2026, 20% in 2027, 30% from 2028). A carbon price effectively paid in India (e.g. CCTS) may be deductible for actual-data declarations once the Commission's rules are final.
key: Exporter actions: map products to CN codes; set up installation-level MRV (direct + indirect emissions, precursors); third-party verification; register installation in the CBAM registry; supply data to EU customers; compare default vs verified cost
Overlaps: CCTS verified reports, ISO 14064, GHG Protocol; free allocation deduction shrinks to 2034

key: Design-stage compliance: envelope, HVAC, lighting, renewable share; third-party certification
Interacts with EIA 2006 Item 8 and state green-building incentives

t: Ozone Depleting Substances (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 (as amended) & Kigali HFC phase-down
sum: Controls production, import, sale and use of ODS (CFCs banned; HCFC-22 phase-out schedule to 2030; HCFC-141b banned in foams since 2020). India ratified the Kigali Amendment (2021): HFC consumption freeze 2028 and phase-down to 2047. Refrigerant leaks count as Scope 1 GHG (GWP-weighted) in CCTS/BRSR inventories.
key: Servicing of refrigeration/AC with recovery units; technician training (good practices); record refrigerant purchases/leaks for GHG inventory
Fire suppression: halon banned; alternatives (clean agents) with GWP considerations

t: Industrial Relations Code, 2020
sum: In force 21 Nov 2025; subsumes the Industrial Disputes Act, Trade Unions Act and Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act. Relevant to safety governance: standing orders (300+ workers) must cover safety rules and discipline; grievance redressal committees; works committees (100+); negotiating union recognition; strike notice (14 days) and lay-off/retrenchment provisions that affect shutdown safety planning.
key: Standing orders define duties, shift working, disciplinary action for safety violations
Grievance committee (20+ workers) – channel for safety complaints

a: BIS; API; OISD; US EPA; PESO (licensing in India)
sum: IS 803 – vertical mild-steel welded oil storage tanks (design/erection); IS 10987 – horizontal cylindrical underground/above-ground tanks for petroleum products (retail outlets, site fuel storage); API 650 design, API 653 in-service inspection (external every 5 years, internal per corrosion rate, max 20 years), API 2000 venting, API 2350 overfill protection, API 2015/2016 tank entry & cleaning, API 1615 UST installation, API 1604 UST closure; OISD-STD-118 layouts/spacing, OISD-STD-129 inspection of storage tanks, OISD-STD-244 depots and terminals; US 40 CFR Part 280 underground storage tank rules (leak detection, corrosion protection, financial responsibility) – the most complete UST regime to benchmark.
key: Dyke/bund: capacity for largest tank (Petroleum Rules 2002 / OISD-118: ≥ 100% of largest tank + dead stock; 110% common practice); bund height ≤ 2 m typical

UST: double-wall or lined single-wall with interstitial monitoring, automatic tank gauging, cathodic protection for steel, precision tightness test on installation and periodically, inventory reconciliation; vapour recovery Stage I/II where CPCB mandates
Decommissioning: empty, clean, gas-free, inert fill or removal, soil/groundwater sampling, PESO licence surrender

t: IS 7689 – Guide for control of undesirable static electricity; NFPA 77; IS/IEC 60079 (hazardous area classification)
sum: Static ignition is a leading cause of tank-truck, drum-filling and solvent-handling fires. Bonding/earthing of all conductive parts, limiting flow velocity (≤ 1 m/s until fill pipe submerged, ≤ 7 m/s thereafter), relaxation time, no splash filling, conductive hoses, anti-static clothing/footwear in Zone 1, and classification of areas (Zone 0/1/2 gas; 20/21/22 dust) with Ex-rated equipment.
key: Earth resistance for static bonding ≤ 10 Ω (static), overall earthing per IS 3043
Verify bonding clamps before each transfer; interlock bonding with pump start on loading gantries

t: PNGRB Regulations – Technical Standards & Specifications incl. Safety (T4S) for pipelines, CGD networks, LNG terminals; ERDMP Regulations 2010; Integrity Management
a: Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB)
sum: Mandatory for natural-gas and petroleum pipelines, city-gas distribution (CNG stations, PNG networks) and LNG facilities: design, construction, operation, maintenance, emergency response and disaster management plans (ERDMP), third-party audits, right-of-way safety, excavation near pipelines (contractor duty to obtain pipeline operator clearance).
key: Construction contractors: pipeline locating and permit before digging near RoW; ROU markers
CGD/CNG stations: safety distances, gas detection, ESD, dispenser interlocks

t: IS 4263 (Code of safety for chlorine), IS 4544 (Code of safety for ammonia), Chlorine Institute pamphlets, IIAR standards (ammonia refrigeration), OSHA PSM thresholds
sum: Design and handling codes for the two most common toxic gases on Indian industrial sites (water treatment, textiles, chemicals, cold storage, fertilizer). Both are MSIHC Schedule chemicals: toxic-release scenarios drive on-site/off-site emergency plans. Chlorine tonners handled under Gas Cylinders Rules; bulk ammonia under SMPV(U).
key: Chlorine: emergency kits A/B/C, scrubber/neutralisation, SCBA, leak detectors, wind sock, 1 ppm TLV / 0.5 ppm (ACGIH); IDLH 10 ppm
Ammonia: 25 ppm TLV, 35 ppm STEL, IDLH 300 ppm; machinery-room ventilation and detection (IIAR 2), ESD valves, water deluge

t: Combustible dust: NFPA 652 (fundamentals, Dust Hazard Analysis), NFPA 654 / 61 / 484 / 664 / 68 / 69; OSHA Combustible Dust NEP (CPL 03-00-008); ATEX 1999/92/EC; IEC 60079-10-2; Factories Act s.37 via state rules
sum: Flour, sugar, starch, wood, textiles fibre, coal, aluminium/magnesium, pharmaceutical powders and plastics all form explosive clouds. Requirements: Dust Hazard Analysis (NFPA 652, revalidated every 5 years), housekeeping limits (layer thickness > 0.8 mm / 1/32 in over 5% of area is a deflagration hazard), explosion venting (NFPA 68) or suppression/isolation (NFPA 69), bonding, dust collectors sited outdoors or with venting, Zone 20/21/22 equipment (IEC 60079-10-2), hot-surface limits, no compressed-air blow-down.
key: India: Factories Act s.37 (explosive or inflammable dust/gas) continues via state Factories Rules and OSH Code s.6; MSIHC for flammable solids
Kst/Pmax testing of dusts (ASTM E1226) to size vents

t: Lifting tackles & rigging: IS 2266 (steel wire ropes), IS 6216 (chain slings), IS 3832 (hand-operated chain pulley blocks), ISO 4309 (wire rope care & discard), EN 13155 / EN 13889 / EN 1677, ASME B30.9 / B30.10 / B30.20 / B30.26; Factories Act s.29 & BOCW rules (test & examination)
a: BIS; ISO; CEN; ASME; state factory inspectorates (competent persons)
sum: Design, marking (SWL/WLL, ID), proof-load testing, periodic thorough examination and discard criteria for slings, chains, shackles, hooks, eyebolts, spreader beams, chain blocks and winches. India: Factories Act s.29 (via state rules) – test and thorough examination by competent person at least every 12 months with register; BOCW Central/state rules – lifting gear tested before first use and examined at least every 6 months (verify); UK LOLER – 6-monthly for accessories and lifting persons.
key: Discard: wire rope (ISO 4309) – broken wires above table limit (e.g. 6 in one lay length for 6-strand ropes), diameter reduction > 7–10%, kinks, corrosion, birdcaging; chain – stretch > 5%, wear > 10%, cracks; hooks – throat opening increase > 15%, twist > 10°; shackles – pin wear > 10%; webbing slings – cut, label missing, chemical/heat damage
Colour-code quarterly; quarantine failed gear; unique ID traceable to certificate

t: Cranes: IS 3177 (EOT & gantry cranes), IS 807 (crane structures), IS 4573 (mobile cranes), IS 13367 Pt 1 (safe use), OSHA 1926.1400–1442 & 1926.1435 (tower cranes), 1910.179, ASME B30.2 / B30.3 / B30.5, BS 7121 Pts 1–5, BS EN 14439 (tower cranes), BS EN 13000 (mobile cranes)
a: BIS; OSHA; ASME; BSI/CEN; state inspectorates
sum: Design, erection, inspection and operation standards for mobile, crawler, tower and overhead cranes. Tower cranes: foundation/tie design by manufacturer or engineer, erection/climbing/dismantling by trained crew under supervision, anti-collision and zoning on multi-crane sites, out-of-service free-slew in storms, anemometer limits (manufacturer; stop lifting typically 9–10 m/s), lightning protection, test after each erection by competent person, daily/weekly/monthly inspection schedules. EOT cranes: limit switches (hoist upper, travel), brakes, pendant/remote control checks, gantry rail alignment, load test at 125% after major repair.
key: India: 12-monthly competent-person test/examination (Factories Act s.29 via state rules; BOCW rules); certificate in cab; operator competence (HMV for mobile); IS 13367 hand signals
OSHA: operator certification (1926.1427), assembly/disassembly director, power-line Table A clearances, ground conditions, annual & monthly inspections (1926.1412)

t: Hand & power tools: OSHA 1926 Subpart I (1926.300–307) & 1910 Subpart P (1910.241–244); UK PUWER 1998 & HSG17 (abrasive wheels); ANSI B7.1; ANSI A10.3 (powder-actuated); IS/IEC 62841 (power tool safety); IS 9474 (guarding)
sum: Guarding of portable tools (grinder guard, retractable saw guards), abrasive-wheel mounting/speed/inspection (ring test; only trained persons mount wheels), powder-actuated tool operator training and licensing, pneumatic tool whip-checks and ≤ 30 psi for cleaning (never on clothing), electrical tool double insulation/RCD/PAT, hand tool condition (no mushroomed heads, split handles), inspection colour-coding, tool registers and quarantine of defective tools.
key: India: state Factories Rules (grinding wheel safety provisions – verify rule), BOCW rules (tools), CEA regs and IS 732 for portable electrical equipment; check current BIS Quality Control Orders before importing power tools

t: Forklifts & warehousing: OSHA 1910.178 (powered industrial trucks), ASME B56.1, 1910.176 (materials storage), NFPA 13/NBC Part 4 (high-piled storage), EN 15635 (racking inspection), SEMA guidance; India MV Act (registered FLTs), Factories Act via rules
sum: Operator training & evaluation every 3 years (OSHA), pre-use inspection, capacity plate and load centre (600 mm / 24 in), attachments de-rating, seat belts, pedestrian segregation, speed limits, battery charging rooms (hydrogen ventilation, acid, eyewash), LPG forklifts (PESO cylinders, indoor CO), racking: SWL signage, damage classification (green/amber/red), weekly visual, annual expert inspection, aisle widths, sprinkler clearance (≥ 450 mm / 18 in), block-stacking stability.
key: India: forklifts on public roads need RTO registration and HMV/LMV licence; inside factory – authorisation, medical fitness, Factories Act s.7A duty
Dock levellers, wheel chocks, vehicle keys control during loading

t: Machinery safety: ISO 12100, ISO 13849-1 / IEC 62061 (safety-related controls, PL/SIL), ISO 14120 (guards), ISO 13857 (safety distances), ISO 10218-1/-2 (industrial robots), ISO/TS 15066 (cobots), EU Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 (from 20 Jan 2027), IS 9474, Factories Act ss.21–33 via state rules
a: ISO/IEC; European Commission; BIS; state inspectorates
sum: Risk assessment and reduction for machinery; guard design and reach distances; interlocking (ISO 14119); performance level of safety functions (e-stops, light curtains, two-hand controls); robot cells (perimeter guarding, safeguarded space, collaborative operation limits); presses (ANSI B11 series), woodworking, conveyors; CE/EHSR documentation for imported machines; India: fencing, machinery in motion, young persons, self-acting machines (legacy Factories Act sections continued via OSH Code s.6 and state rules).
key: Buy-in checklist: declaration of conformity, risk assessment, manuals in English/local language, safety circuit category, guard interlocks
Periodic functional test of safety devices; LOTO for maintenance

t: Foundry & hot-metal safety: state Factories Rules dangerous-operations schedules (foundry operations, sand-blasting, lead, chrome), DGFASLI/CLI foundry guidance, HSE UK 'Foundries' guidance (molten metal, cupolas, induction furnaces), OSHA 1910 (silica 1910.1053, 1910.94, 1910.132), EN ISO 11612 / ASTM F955 (molten-metal PPE)
a: State inspectorates (KA DFBISH / TN DISH); DGFASLI; HSE; OSHA; BIS
sum: No single Indian foundry code: obligations flow from the Factories Act (now OSH Code) dangerous-operations schedules in the Karnataka and Tamil Nadu Factories Rules (medical examination, PPE, exhaust ventilation, washing facilities for foundry, lead, chrome, sand-blasting operations), exposure limits (Schedule II: silica, CO, manganese, lead, formaldehyde, phenol), and general duties. International guidance covers molten-metal explosions (water contact), furnace water-cooling failures, ladle/crane integrity, cupola charging, induction-furnace lining, fettling (silica, noise, HAV), binder chemicals (phenolic resins, isocyanates, amines in cold-box), heat stress and burns.
key: Molten metal: dry charge and ladles (preheat ≥ 100 °C), no water/moisture near pouring, ladle lifting gear inspected daily and tested 6-monthly, dedicated hot-metal routes, splash PPE (aluminised), face shields, spats, metatarsal boots
Silica: wet/LEV sand handling, enclosed shakeout, respirators (P3), medical surveillance (chest X-ray/spirometry) – silicosis notifiable (OSH Code s.12)
Induction furnace: water-cooling monitoring with interlock/alarm, earth-leakage detection on coil, lining wear monitoring; cupola: CO monitoring, charging door interlocks
note: Coimbatore, Belagavi, Shimoga, Chennai (Ambattur) clusters: DISH/DFBISH run periodic foundry safety drives; expect inspection focus on silica, molten-metal PPE and crane certificates.

t: Dangerous operations schedules – Karnataka Factories Rules 1969 (Rule 129 schedules) & Tamil Nadu Factories Rules 1950 (Rule 95 schedules I–XX)
a: DFBISH Karnataka; DISH Tamil Nadu (certifying surgeons)
sum: Both states list operations where special rules apply (pre-employment and periodic medical examination by certifying surgeon, exposure controls, PPE, washing/cloakrooms, prohibition of food, health registers). Typical schedules: manufacture of aerated water; electrolytic plating; lead and lead compounds; manufacture/use of chromium compounds; sand-blasting; cellulose/solvent spraying; grinding/glazing of metals; foundry operations; glass manufacture; pottery; carbon disulphide; benzene; pesticides; asbestos (TN Schedule XX substituted 2025); cotton dust (byssinosis); rubber; chlorine; pickling; compressed air work; nitro/amino compounds; manufacture of rayon; highly flammable liquids and gases.
key: Medical examination records in prescribed forms; certificate of fitness; removal from work on medical advice; occupational-disease notice (OSH Code s.12)
Transition: schedules continue until state OSH rules replace them; OSH Code Ch. XII and Central Rules list similar 'hazardous processes'
note: Schedule numbers differ between the two states and are amended (TN 2025); cite the current gazetted schedule in medical surveillance SOPs.

t: HT & substation safety: CEA Safety Regulations 2023 (work on live/dead lines, permits, earthing), IS 5216, IS 3043, IS 10028 (transformers), IEC 61936-1 (power installations > 1 kV), IEEE 1584 (arc-flash calculation), NFPA 70E (boundaries & PPE), IS 1646 (electrical installations fire safety), IS 732
sum: Covers authorisation of competent persons, HT permit-to-work (isolate–lock–test–earth–tag), approach distances, arc-flash incident energy study and labelling, transformer fire protection and oil containment, SF6 handling, cable trench fire stopping, battery rooms, substation access control and periodic inspection by the Electrical Inspector.
key: NFPA 70E approach boundaries (verify Table 130.4): 50–150 V – limited 1.07 m, restricted avoid contact; 151–750 V – limited 1.07 m, restricted 0.3 m; 751 V–15 kV – limited 1.52 m, restricted 0.66 m; arc-flash boundary from study (1.2 cal/cm²)
Electrical accident report to Electrical Inspector within 48 h (Form A); periodic inspection of HT installations (yearly/5-yearly per state CEIG rules)

t: Batteries, ESS, solar PV & EV charging: NFPA 855, UL 9540 / 9540A, IEC 62619 / IEC 62933-5-2, IS 16046 (Li-ion safety), IEC 62446-1 & IS/IEC 60364-7-712 (PV installations), IS 14286 / IS 61730 (module QCO), CEA Technical Standards (connectivity of distributed generation; EV charging safety in CEA 2023 regs), Battery Waste Management Rules 2022, IEEE 1635 / IS 1651 (lead-acid rooms)
sum: Lithium-ion energy storage: thermal-runaway risk, spacing, enclosures, fire detection (off-gas/early), suppression and deflagration venting (NFPA 855 / UL 9540A test data), state-of-charge limits for storage/transport (UN 38.3 / 30% SoC), end-of-life handling under Battery Waste Rules. Lead-acid rooms: hydrogen ventilation (keep < 1% v/v), acid-resistant floors, eyewash, insulated tools. Solar PV: DC arc hazards (no load break on DC without isolators), rooftop fall risk and fragile roofs, module cleaning at height, inverter rooms, lightning/surge protection, firefighter DC isolation signage. EV charging: CEA safety provisions, RCD type B, emergency stop, ventilation for indoor charging.
key: MNRE/BIS QCO: modules and inverters must carry BIS certification (ALMM list for government projects)
Rooftop solar installers fall under BOCW/OSH Code work-at-height duties

t: Fire protection systems: IS 13039 (external hydrants), IS 15105 (sprinklers), IS 2189 (detection & alarm), IS 3844 (high-rise), IS 1641 / 1642 / 1644 (fire safety of buildings – general, materials, exits), IS 2190 / IS 15683 (extinguishers), IS 12349 (industrial fire protection), IS 15325 (fixed foam), NFPA 25 (inspection, testing & maintenance), NFPA 13/14/20/72, Tariff Advisory Committee (TAC) rules (insurance)
a: BIS; NFPA; State Fire Services (KSFES / TNFRS); insurers (TAC/IRDAI)
sum: Design and maintenance basis behind Fire NOCs and insurance. Typical test cadence: fire pumps weekly run (churn), annual flow test; sprinkler/hydrant systems quarterly inspections, annual full test, 5-yearly internal inspection; detectors tested annually, panels weekly; extinguishers monthly visual, annual service, hydrostatic test 3–5 years (CO2/clean agent 10 years); emergency lighting monthly flick/annual duration; fire doors quarterly; foam concentrate annual lab test.
key: Fire water: 2–4 h reserve for industrial risks (TAC/NBC), fire pumps diesel + electric + jockey, hydrant spacing ≤ 45 m (industrial) / 30 m (high-hazard)
Impairment procedure when systems are out of service: notify fire brigade/insurer, fire watch, hot-work ban

t: Tunnelling & compressed-air work: BOCW Central Rules 1998 (tunnelling chapter), OSHA 1926 Subpart S (1926.800–804; 1926.803 compressed air), BS 6164 (safety in tunnelling), UK Work in Compressed Air Regulations 1996, ITA guidelines, DGMS (where mines)
a: OSHA; BSI; ITA; state labour departments; DGMS
sum: Ground support, ventilation (≥ 200 cfm/person; ≥ 30 ft/min air velocity OSHA), continuous gas monitoring (methane < 10% LEL action; CO, H2S, O2), check-in/check-out, communication, refuge chambers, fire protection of TBMs, hoisting in shafts, flooding/inrush precautions, compressed-air work (medical lock, decompression tables, medical surveillance), diesel exhaust control.
key: Metro/road tunnel contracts in Bengaluru/Chennai follow Central BOCW rules + employer specifications (BMRCL/CMRL safety manuals)

t: Piling & deep foundations: BS EN 16228 (drilling & foundation equipment), FPS guidance, IS 2911 (pile foundations), OSHA 1926 Subparts N/CC (cranes), BOCW rules (excavation/foundations)
a: CEN; Federation of Piling Specialists (UK); BIS; OSHA
sum: Rig stability (platform working-platform certificate), exclusion zones around augers/rotating parts (entanglement – no loose clothing; auger cleaners), rebar cage lifting, tremie concrete, open bore covers, bentonite handling and disposal, noise/vibration limits near structures, overhead lines.
key: Working platform (piling mat) design and sign-off before rig entry; daily checks after rain
Sheet piling: vibro/impact hammer exclusion, trench collapse precautions

t: Blasting: Explosives Rules 2008, IS 4081 (blasting & drilling in construction), DGMS Technical Circular 7/1997 (ground vibration limits), DGMS blasting regulations (Metalliferous Mines Regs 1961 / Coal Mines Regs 2017), OSHA 1926 Subpart U
sum: Licensed magazine (Form LE-3/LE-5), licensed shot-firer/blaster, explosives van and daily issue/return register, blasting plan (burden, spacing, charge per delay, initiation), ground-vibration monitoring (PPV limits per DGMS circular by structure type and frequency), flyrock control (stemming, mats), warning sirens and shelters, misfire procedure, police/DM intimation and timing restrictions near habitation.
key: DGMS PPV limits (mm/s, verify): domestic structures not owned by operator – 5 (< 8 Hz), 10 (8–25 Hz), 15 (> 25 Hz); industrial buildings – 10/20/25; historical monuments – 2/5/10
Misfire wait: electric ≥ 5–30 min, fuse ≥ 30–60 min (per rules); only shot-firer approaches

t: Working over/near water & marine works: IS 13416 Pt 5 (prevention of drowning), Dock Workers (Safety, Health & Welfare) Regulations 1990 (via OSH Code), Merchant Shipping Act 1958 (vessels/barges), ILO C152 (dock work), OSHA 1926.106 (working over or near water) / 1917 / 1918, UK HSE guidance (rescue boats, lifejackets EN ISO 12402)
a: DGFASLI Dock Safety; Ports; DG Shipping; OSHA
sum: Lifejackets (buoyancy ≥ 150 N for work-wear), lifebuoys with 30 m line every 60 m, rescue boat with trained crew on standby, edge protection/nets, tide and current planning, barge stability and crane limits afloat, man-overboard drill, hypothermia/current hazards, water-borne disease.
key: Jetty, bridge pier and intake works in Chennai/Ennore/Mangaluru/Karwar fall under port and coastal regulations (CRZ clearance)

t: Laboratory safety: OSHA 1910.1450 (Laboratory Standard – Chemical Hygiene Plan), NABL/ISO 17025 safety clauses, OECD GLP, DBT Biosafety Guidelines (BSL levels), Bio-Medical Waste Rules 2016, IS 15656 (hazard identification)
sum: Chemical hygiene plan, fume hood face velocity (0.4–0.5 m/s), chemical storage segregation, peroxide-formers dating, cryogenics, compressed gases, glassware under vacuum/pressure, biosafety cabinets and BSL-2 practices for microbiology labs, sharps and bio-medical waste segregation (colour-coded bags, autoclaving), emergency shower/eyewash.
key: QC labs in chemical/pharma plants fall under Factories/OSH Code hazardous-process rules as well

t: Biological hazards: OSHA 1910.1030 (bloodborne pathogens), Epidemic Diseases Act 1897 (as amended 2020), Bio-Medical Waste Rules 2016, MoHFW/ICMR advisories, IS 10500 (drinking water), ASHRAE 188 / HSE L8 (legionella)
a: MoHFW; State Health Departments; CPCB; OSHA; ASHRAE/HSE
sum: Pandemic/outbreak readiness (state powers under the Epidemic Diseases Act), vector control at sites and camps (dengue, malaria, chikungunya – monsoon), water-borne disease prevention (potable water to IS 10500, tested monthly), snake/scorpion/dog bite protocols (antivenom/rabies PEP hospital identified), tetanus prophylaxis, needle-stick/bloodborne precautions in OHCs, legionella control in cooling towers and hot-water systems (temperature regimes, biocide, monthly inspection, quarterly sampling where risk).
key: Construction camps: ULB/Health Department inspections; fogging, larvicide, drainage
OHC bio-medical waste: authorisation and common facility tie-up

t: Site security & public safety: Private Security Agencies (Regulation) Act 2005, POSH Act 2013, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (workplace crimes), IRC:SP:55 (public interface), NDMA guidelines, municipal hoarding/barricade bye-laws
a: State Home Departments (PSARA licensing); Police; ULBs
sum: Licensed security agency (PSARA) with verified guards; access control (biometric/RFID), visitor management, CCTV retention, perimeter integrity, material gate passes, public protection from falling objects and traffic (hoardings, covered walkways, debris nets), workplace-violence and harassment prevention (ICC under POSH, grievance channels), threat/bomb-call procedure, labour unrest and lock-out safety, cash/explosives/fuel security.
key: Night security of cranes/hoists (power isolated, keys controlled); theft of scaffold components creates collapse risk
Media/public communication during incidents via single spokesperson

t: Drone Rules, 2021 (as amended) – DGCA / Digital Sky
sum: Drones used for progress survey, façade/roof/stack/flare/chimney inspection and confined-area reconnaissance must have a UIN (type-certified), remote pilot certificate (above nano/micro non-commercial), flight only in green zones or with permission (yellow/red zones – airports, defence, state secretariats), ≤ 120 m AGL, visual line of sight, no flight over crowds, insurance, and operator SOP; incident reporting to DGCA.
key: Site rule: exclusion of persons under flight path; battery (Li-Po) charging/storage controls; data privacy of imagery

t: Road works & bitumen: IRC:SP:55 (traffic management in work zones), IRC:SP:98 / MoRTH Specifications (bituminous works), CPCB/TNPCB/KSPCB hot-mix plant siting & emission norms, HSE/Eurobitume 'Safe handling of bitumen' guidance, Petroleum Rules (cutback/kerosene), MV Act
sum: Work-zone layout (advance warning, transition, buffer, work and termination areas), flaggers, night lighting/retro-reflective PPE, plant reversing control, bitumen burns (hot bitumen 150–180 °C; never water into hot bitumen; cool burns with water, do not remove bitumen from skin), tanker transfer earthing, fume control at pavers/HMP, cutback solvent flammability, HMP siting ≥ 500 m from habitation (state norms – verify) with dust/stack controls.
key: Emulsion vs cutback: prefer emulsions to reduce fire risk
Burn kit and burns-centre tie-up for bitumen crews

t: IS 17893:2023 – Work Permit System — Code of Practice
sum: National benchmark for permit-to-work systems, covering seven distinct permits: Cold Work, Hot Work, Confined Space, Excavation, Electrical, Work at Height and Radiography. Annex C gives the confined-space entry permit format and gas-testing log (Oxygen 19.5–23.5%; LEL < 5%, 0% for hot work).
key: Roles: permit issuer, receiver, gas tester, isolation authority; validity, extension, suspension, close-out

Companion standards: OISD-STD-105 (oil & gas), IS 818 / IS 3016 (welding & cutting), IS 11006 (flashback arrestors), IS 5216 (electrical work), IS 11972 (sewer/confined space), IS 10245 (breathing apparatus)

t: Tamil Nadu Control of Industrial Major Accident Hazards (CIMAH) Rules, 1994
a: DISH Tamil Nadu (Chief Inspector of Factories)
sum: State rules under the Factories Act for Major Accident Hazard (MAH) units: notification of sites, safety reports, third-party safety audits, on-site emergency plans and inputs to the District Collector's off-site plan. Operate alongside MSIHC Rules 1989 (under the EP Act) and continue in transition under the OSH Code.
key: Third-party safety audit periodicity and auditor recognition by DISH
Information to the public; mock drills with the District Crisis Group

t: Major Accident Hazards Control (Karnataka) Rules, 1994
a: DFBISH / FBISH Karnataka (Chief Inspector of Factories)
sum: Karnataka's MAH control rules under the Factories Act: site notification, safety report, safety audit, on-site emergency plan and off-site plan inputs for installations above threshold quantities. Read with MSIHC Rules 1989 and the Karnataka Factories (Safety Audit) Rules 2024 (periodic safety audits by accredited auditors for hazardous factories).
key: Safety report updates on modification; audit findings closure reported to the Chief Inspector

t: BOCW (Karnataka Amendment) Rules, 2024
a: Labour Department Karnataka; FBISH; alongside BBMP/BDA bylaws
sum: 2024 amendment to the Building and Other Construction Workers (Karnataka) Rules, 2006 — enforced by FBISH and the Labour Department. Verify the amended provisions (registration, welfare, safety chapters) on the Labour Department gazette before citing.
key: Read with Karnataka BOCW Rules 2006 technical chapters and OSH Code Ch. XIII

t: Karnataka Boiler Rules, 1982
a: Chief Inspector of Boilers, FBISH Karnataka
sum: State boiler rules (registration, inspection fees, attendants, repairs) under the Boilers Act — now read with the Boilers Act 2025 and Indian Boiler Regulations 1950.

t: Tamil Nadu Boiler Rules (Directorate of Boilers, Tamil Nadu)
sum: State boiler rules administered by the Directorate of Boilers (registration, annual inspection, boiler attendants/BOE examinations, repairers) under the Boilers Act 2025 / IBR 1950.

t: BIS industrial-hygiene & electrical safety codes: IS 3103 (industrial ventilation), IS 6665 (industrial lighting), IS 7194 (noise exposure assessment), IS 15652 (insulating mats), IS 10592 (emergency showers & eyewash), IS 4209 (chemical labs/plants), IS 11457 Pt 1 (fire safety of chemical plants), IS 17859 (GHS classification, labelling & SDS)
sum: Standards that give the technical content behind state Factories Rules on ventilation (TN Rule 17 / KA Rule 19), lighting, noise, electrical panel protection, emergency showers and chemical plant fire safety; IS 17859 aligns Indian SDS/labels with UN GHS.
key: IS 15652 insulating mats replace IS 5424 — required in front of all LT/HT panels
IS 7194 supports hearing-conservation programmes (85 dB(A) action level)

t: BIS construction safety series (CED 46) & SP 70: IS 8989 (concrete-framed structures), IS 5121 (piling), IS 5916 (hot bituminous work), IS 13415 (protective barriers), IS 5175 & IS 11057 (safety nets), IS 11972 (sewer/confined space), IS 10245 Pts 1–4 (SCBA/airline), IS 11006 (flashback arrestors), IS 16819 (machinery safety design), IS 1991 Pts 1–10 (grinding wheels), IS 2762 (wire-rope slings)
sum: Additional Indian Standards referenced by the state matrix: SP 70 (2001) BIS Handbook on Construction Safety Practices; formwork/centering, piling, bitumen, barriers, nets, breathing apparatus, flashback arrestors, machinery design, abrasive wheels and wire-rope slings.

t: BIS PPE certification set (ISI mark required under TN Rule 61-O / KA Rule 65 & 88): IS 2925, IS 15298 Pts 2–4, IS 5983 & IS 8520, IS 6994, IS 4770 & IS 13774, IS 9167 & IS 6229, IS 9473, IS 15322, IS 15809, IS 15748, IS 10592
sum: Helmets; safety footwear; eye protectors; mechanical gloves; electrical insulating gloves; hearing protectors; filtering half masks; gas filters and combined cartridges; high-visibility clothing; heat & flame protective clothing; emergency showers and eyewash stations.
